reason: On this branch's build the machine side holds: ORA (zp),Y/TAY/BEQ/BNE are all NMOS opcodes, the new loop sits in &DF53-&DF6C (no branch or code page crossing, branches in range), the (s_ptr),Y reads are the same addresses so the same crossings, no self-modified operands here, and the count is right: clean row of n bytes 15n-1 -> 13n+2 (n>=2; n=1 14 -> 17), so with the window's measured 14.07 bytes in 2.3 rows a pass old 210.2 -> new ~188.9, ~21.2 a pass, ~9.2 a row; bytes +8 (9 -> 17). It is refuted on the bytes: the +8 lands at the end of hazel_b, which on the gameplay disc is full. build/strykers-gameplay.lst (built 2026-10-23 01:23, the hud-rupture/gameplay line) has sky_col_check at &DF4A followed by level_movers_x_low, ground_columns and rup_k_lo/hi with hazel_b_end = &DFFF: 1 byte free, so +8 fails game.6502's ASSERT hazel_b_end <= &E000 by 7 when this grind is merged there (and moves ground_columns/level tables read in play). The relies_on claim that sky_col_check is the last code in hazel_b with nothing after it is false for that build. Secondarily the dirty path loses its early exit: a dirty row now reads to its end before BNE dirty (up to ~+100 cycles a call, n=8 dirty at the first byte: 8 -> 107); the profile shows it 0.0 a pass, but it is a worst-case-frame cost the claim does not count.
